title.narrative: Multi-Donor Trust Fond för stöd till rättsväsendet i Serbien
Multi-Donor Trust Fund for Justice Sector Support

description.narrative: Overall objective is to facilitate Serbia’s justice sector EU integration, establish a justice sector performance framework and strengthen aid coordination in Serbia’s justice sector, by providing focused short-term support to the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) to strengthen its capacity and complete key judicial modernization analyses and actions. It supports three key development challenges for Serbia’s justice sector: strengthening judicial and prosecutorial independence, accountability and efficiency. Outcome objective 1: Improved access to justice in Serbia through more concentrated, transparent and effective legal aid programmes available to all citizens, including women, minorities and vulnerable groups in all regions. Outcome objective 2: Decisions on ICT investments in the Serbian judiciary are made strategically to maximise the effectiveness and efficiency gains and reduce the overall investment costs.
Projektet syftar till att slutföra en insats för införande av rättshjälp i Serbien, kombinerat med ökad biståndseffektivitet genom stöd via en fond där sex andra givare bidrar

Sida will join the WB multi-donor TF fund to support Serbia's justice sector EU integration and strengthen aid coordination in the sector. This project is a continuation of previous free legal aid project that was implemented through UNDP. The main focus is on improving access to justice in Serbia through more concentrated, transparent and effective legal aid programmes available to all citizens.

The main results achieved by the MDTF-JSS during its entire implementation period reflect significant progress in strengthening Serbia's judicial system and facilitating its integration into the European Union. Over its lifespan, the project has proved instrumental in Serbia's justice reform process by improving institutional capacities, enhancing the efficiency and quality of justice services, and increasing access to justice. These achievements are confirmed by gradual improvements in international Rule of Law ratings and positive public perceptions.
The key results and outcomes are detailed below:
1. Improvements in judicial efficiency and case management: The efforts supported by the MDTF-JSS resulted in improvements in court efficiency, including the introduction of streamlined judicial procedures and the reduction of backlogs:
• Reduction in disposition time: The total disposition time reduced significantly from 580 days in 2014 to 217 in 2023,
• Backlog reduction: The support provided helped reduce the stock of pending cases from 2.85 million in 2014 to 1.10 million in 2023,
• System Implementation: This efficiency was facilitated by the introduction of the case management system in all courts in 2012, which improved case management and strengthened transparency.
2. Enhanced Rule of Law and public trust: The reform outcomes supported by the MDTF-JSS are reflected in positive trends in international rankings and public perception:
• International rankings: Serbias percentile rank on the Rule of Law in Worldwide Governance Indicators increased from 37.5 out of 100 in 2008 to 51.4 out of 100 in 2023,
• Public perception: Public trust in the judicial system significantly increased to 55% in 2020, compared to figures reported in 2009 and 2013,
• Civil justice access: The score measuring the accessibility and affordability of civil justice increased from 0.48 in 20122013 to 0.57 in 2024. The effectiveness of civil justice enforcement saw a comparable rise, from a score of 0.38 to 0.51.
3. Key legislative and institutional reforms: The project provided inputs necessary for drafting and implementing significant legal frameworks, contributing to broader goals of independence and access to justice:
• Constitutional and legislative alignment: The MDTF-JSS activities contributed to the implementation of the second-generation reforms aimed at improving judicial independence and accountability. For example, the project supported efforts that gave practical effect to the 2022 Constitutional amendments, resulting in the successful restructuring and Constitution of the High Judicial Council (HJC) and High Prosecutorial Council (HPC) in 2023,
• Access to legal aid: The project supported the preparation and implementation of the Law on Free Legal Aid in 2019. This framework aims to increase social inclusion by providing free legal aid requests to eligible persons, such as vulnerable groups and those receiving social benefits.
4. Strategic planning, analytical underpinning, and capacity building: The MDTF-JSS has established a strong foundation for evidence-based decision-making and strengthened institutional capacity across the justice sector:
• Strategic policy formulation: The Fund has continuously informed judicial reform strategy, monitoring and evaluation. It supported the development and adoption of the National Judicial Reform Strategy (NJRS) for 2013-2018. It provided direct inputs into drafting the Action Plan for Chapter 23 (for the EU Accession Process) and its revisions.
• Major analytical outputs: The MDTF-JSS produced key analytical inputs, including the 2014 Judicial Functional Review and the subsequent 2021 Serbia Judicial Functional Review, which benchmarked progress and informed subsequent second-generation judicial reforms.
• Capacity development: More than 2,000 public sector employees and staff were trained in EU accession in justice areas. Capacity improvements were seen in areas such as performance management and human resource planning.
• Targeted assessments (Phase 3): During the final phase, targeted studies were developed, informing future work. One example is the Commercial Courts Needs Assessment, which identified challenges and formulated recommendations for improving commercial courts, and the Human Resource Analysis conducted for the HJC and HPC.
5. Enhanced aid effectiveness and donor coordination: The governance and mechanism of the MDTF-JSS proved to be a successful strategic tool for managing external assistance in the sector:
• Coordination platform: Through structures like the Partners' Forum and Management Committee meetings, the project enhanced dialogue and provided a platform for donor coordination.
• Resource mobilization: This cooperation facilitated increased aid effectiveness, resulting in Serbia securing additional resources for reforms, including 30 million EUR in direct budget support from the EU in 2022.
• Flexibility and ownership: The flexible structure allowed the implementing Bank team to deliver integrated and timely expertise tailored to client needs. The approach fostered strong ownership among key stakeholders, contributing to the greater sustainability of reform outcomes.
